---
title: "Focus album"
---

```{python}
import duckdb
from IPython.display import display

con = duckdb.connect("../data/processed/music_life.duckdb", read_only=True)
album = con.execute("""
SELECT a.album_id, a.title, ar.name AS artist, a.original_release_date,
       a.spotify_url
FROM albums a
LEFT JOIN artists ar USING (artist_id)
WHERE a.is_focus_album
ORDER BY a.original_release_date
LIMIT 1
""").df()
display(album)

if len(album):
    album_id = int(album.iloc[0]["album_id"])
    tracks = con.execute("""
    SELECT t.track_number, t.track_title,
           r.spotify_url, r.spotify_verified
    FROM album_tracks t
    JOIN recordings r USING (recording_id)
    WHERE t.album_id=?
    ORDER BY t.disc_number, t.track_number
    """, [album_id]).df()
    display(tracks)
```

## Research questions

Who wrote, played on and produced this record? Which recording is represented by each track? Which underlying works are involved? Which people recur elsewhere in the artist's career? Which current Spotify album/track best represents each historical entity?

Spotify is an enrichment; it does not define historical identity.
